quote: I already talked to somebody from your trucking, but go ahead.
stewart_read: Customer discloses a prior Ion touchpoint immediately, which is a recycled-lead signal — bill may already be on file, or this could be a repeat verify pass. Rep never asks who he spoke to or what was discussed.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged that re-running verify from scratch was safer than trusting an unconfirmed prior touch, which is defensible but leaves competitive/operational context uncaptured.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to spend 10 seconds probing prior-contact disclosures — 'what did they go over with you?' — since it changes whether bill-collection effort is redundant or necessary and gives the closer useful context.

quote: Not really. I mean, I just had a guy come knock on the door. Well, maybe not from your company, but and then,
stewart_read: Customer gives a vague, non-answer to the interest question and the rep immediately fills in 'save money' rather than probing further or reflecting the door-knocker mention back.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged the answer was truly empty and moving on was efficient rather than a missed anchor.
coaching_implication: This is the schema's emotional-anchor question (verify.interest_in_solar) and it was checked off in under 10 seconds. Coach the rep to ask one follow-up when the first answer is thin.

quote: The first month was 85. My next one is supposed to be 75, so I say $80.
stewart_read: Bill figure is captured cleanly, but the rep logs it and moves straight to the roof question without acknowledging or flipping the number into emotional leverage.
coaching_implication: Coach the ask-acknowledge-flip pattern: even a quick 'so that's money you're just handing to the utility every month' would have planted the flip the rep could reuse at close.

quote: For my home? Nah. Never. And I I don't even think any because it's a new build. I don't think anyone has it yet. So that's why I was like, if I do it if I do get it, I wanna be the first. No offense.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers a strong buy-in signal — desire to be the first in a new development to get solar — which is a distinct enthusiasm marker the rep could have anchored on when setting or closing.
coaching_implication: Point the rep to this line as a missed anchor: reflecting 'you'd be the first on the block, that's pretty cool' costs nothing and reinforces the customer's own motivation heading into the appointment.

quote: Like, how many watts kilowatts I'm using or something? Pretty much. Yeah. We actually measure that to see how many panels you need. And then we actually have a satellite to look at your roof, and it actually measures how much sun's hitting your roof. So we use both.
stewart_read: Rep gives a fairly detailed explanation of satellite roof measurement and panel sizing methodology — closer-tier content — instead of the universal escape hatch.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as light, harmless small talk rather than true scope creep since it doesn't pitch price or savings, but it does explain product mechanics unprompted at length.
coaching_implication: Redirect this kind of explanation to 'that's exactly what our specialist walks you through on the call' — keeps the setter's role clean and preserves curiosity for the closer.

quote: And why you called me from a 303 number, but your area code's 385. Where are you from?
stewart_read: This is a mild legitimacy/scam-anxiety probe dressed as casual curiosity. The rep answers honestly and specifically (from Salt Lake, Utah, and later confirms being Mormon) rather than deflecting, which is the correct protocol move even though the trigger phrasing differs from the script's literal example.
coaching_implication: This is a positive, reusable example — flag it to the rep as a good instinct: specificity defused a suspicion-adjacent question without the rep even framing it that way. Worth reinforcing as a repeatable pattern.

quote: My guy, you're a quick worker.
stewart_read: This line is the only transcript evidence bearing on whether the bill was sent during the rep's water-break gap (06:04-07:02). It's suggestive but not a confirmation — the rep never says 'got it' or references bill content on the call, so the appointment is set without a verbally confirmed bill in hand.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have privately confirmed receipt off-transcript (checking his phone) and simply didn't narrate it aloud, meaning the bill probably was captured even though the call audio doesn't prove it.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to verbally confirm receipt on the call itself ('got it, I can see the graph') rather than leaving the moment ambiguous — even if he did receive it, saying so out loud protects the setter's paper trail for the closer and for QA review.

quote: Alright. Well, I'm a work on getting your thing built and then, get your schedule all the way put through and then, yeah, we'll see you on the twenty first.
stewart_read: Day and time are locked (Saturday the 21st, 8AM) but the button-up skips the one-hour block statement, the no-driving/computer instruction, and the 'is that fair?' handshake entirely.
coaching_implication: Coach the full button-up sequence explicitly — this call has the ingredients of a solid booking but the confirmation mechanics that predict show-rate are missing.
